title: Persian Solar Hijri Calendar
intro: The Solar Hijri calendar is a solar calendar used for civil dates in Iran and related traditions. Nowruz, the first day of its year, falls close to the northern spring equinox.
summary: Twelve months form a common year of 365 days or a leap year of 366 days.
origin: Modern civil Solar Hijri month lengths were standardised in the twentieth century. Nowruz itself has a much longer cultural history.
structure: The first six months contain 31 days, the next five contain 30 days, and Esfand contains 29 days in a common year or 30 in a leap year.
diagram_caption: SIX LONG MONTHS  /  FIVE MEDIUM  /  ONE VARIABLE
pattern_note: Months are not determined by lunar sightings. This provider uses the maintained ICU-compatible arithmetic leap corrections to keep the year near the seasonal spring boundary.
history: Official calendar conventions have varied across countries and historical periods; the modern month structure cannot be assumed to apply to older Persian dates.
example: 1 Farvardin usually corresponds to 20 or 21 March in Gregorian notation; the exact correspondence depends on the year and calendar rule.
limits: The implemented arithmetic is not a reconstruction of historical Iranian month lengths before 1304 AP (1925 CE), nor a blanket guarantee of every equinox-based civil decision.
